cases.name: unusual amount and new payee
cases.query: Which policy covers a payment materially higher than the established transaction pattern, particularly to a new payee on a young account?

cases.name: large transfer from recently opened account
cases.query: A recently opened account sent an unusually large transfer to a recipient it has never paid before. What review is required?

cases.name: unsupported payment context
cases.query: The payment purpose, beneficiary relationship, and source of funds are unsupported. What information should I request?

cases.name: alert alone does not justify blocking
cases.query: Can this alert alone justify blocking or reporting the transfer, or should I obtain customer context first?

cases.name: transaction burst within one day
cases.query: Eleven transfers posted within twenty-four hours, several split across smaller payments. Which transaction velocity policy applies?

cases.name: rapid pass-through activity
cases.query: Funds were credited and then quickly dispersed in several outbound transfers. How should I assess this pass-through activity?

cases.name: burst differs from historical pattern
cases.query: The customer suddenly made a rapid burst of transfers unlike their historical pattern. What evidence belongs in the investigation rationale?

cases.name: payment fragmented across same day
cases.query: The customer broke one payment into several smaller wires over the same day. Does this pattern require a velocity review?

cases.name: shared counterparties and direct transactions
cases.query: The origin and destination accounts share several counterparties and have repeated direct transactions. Which network policy applies?

cases.name: value concentrated on one recipient
cases.query: Most of the account outbound value goes to one recipient. How should I assess that concentration?

cases.name: hub account with recurring transfers
cases.query: The graph depicts a hub account connected to many payees, with recurring transfers to the same party. Which guidance covers this?

cases.name: preserve network evidence
cases.query: What account identifiers, counterparty counts, and concentration measures should I preserve when documenting relationship links?

cases.name: cross-border geographic context
cases.query: How should I assess geographic context for a cross-border payment without treating the country name alone as proof of risk?

cases.name: international transfer due diligence
cases.query: An international wire has a UK sender and an overseas recipient. What location-based due diligence and transfer-purpose checks are required?

cases.name: possible sanctions screening match
cases.query: A screening result suggests a possible sanctions match. Which authorized human must review it before any decision is made?

cases.name: unsupported jurisdiction risk claim
cases.query: Can I call the destination high risk based solely on geography when the evidence does not support a sanctions or jurisdiction concern?

cases.name: high risk with insufficient evidence
cases.query: Deterministic risk is high, retrieved evidence is insufficient, and model confidence is low. Does this case require human review?

cases.name: transaction and network signals conflict
cases.query: The transaction activity looks suspicious but the account-network picture looks normal. How should I handle those conflicting signals?

cases.name: automated result is not human approval
cases.query: May an automated recommendation be described as analyst-approved if nobody actually reviewed the case?

cases.name: missing information and failed persistence
cases.query: Information is missing and saving the investigation failed. How must those gaps and persistence failures be reported?
